from 5.0; 3 AGENTS.md's bullet and table row on SHARED.md change by the project's direction alone; 4
TODO.md's two Entities entries are closed as decided; 5 A commit that takes something out of the

what failed in a page, and the reviewing session is given no log; 8 The page's repeated lines are

109. **One package on nuget.org, and Templates.** On 2026-11-11 at about 16:30, after one package
    was chosen for the sibling, the several packages were not favored in 3DEngine either, acceptable
    if they are the best choice there, the preference being one package alone, or two with the
    second holding heavy binaries, and the question put was whether several modules must mean
    several packages too; at about 16:40, among the review's options, one package plus Templates was
    chosen. The review's ground for it. What the split gives, the areas, their layers and the norm's
    test, comes of the projects and not of the packages; a game names 3DEngine alone and no one
    takes a part; fifteen ids are fifteen uploads and listings a publish, five of them 38 minutes
    behind on 2026-11-10 and a half-listed version failing a restore before; and the whole package
    is under 5 MB, so nothing asks a package of binaries. So the areas stay projects, one 3DEngine
    package carries every area's assembly and the natives, 3DEngine.Templates stays apart as dotnet
    new asks, and the thirteen area ids get no further version, the owner unlisting them. Decision
    85's packages at one version, as 235 and the split made them, give way to this. Item 256.

110. **Places far from the origin, the engine draws against the eye and can be told the world
    moved.** Chosen on 2026-11-12 at about 05:40, on the review's question after item 257, among
    positions in doubles throughout, a call for the origin alone, and this, the engine keeping its
    float API, drawing everything against the eye inside, and giving a game a call that moves the
    world's origin by a whole offset with nothing of the light built again. The review's ground.
    What 257 found was no one pass's fault, every vertex, shadow, lookup of a frame before and point
    from the depth standing in world floats, and a rule at the core costs less than a mend a pass,
    with no break of the API where doubles would change every call that takes a place. Item 264 does
    it, and 258's list is its map.

111. **The lighting kept as functions, measured first.** Chosen on 2026-11-12, among this, a
    deferred lighting pass, and keeping the lighting inlined behind caches and workers. Every model
    shader carries the whole lighting today, 1.3 MB of fragment and 12 s of a first compile in the
    voxel game's terrain before its second copy went, and each feature of the light adds to every
    shader. The forward pass stays, the lighting compiled as functions a shader calls and not as a
    copy in each, 255's trial, measured by the compile's time and the frame's; a deferred pass is
    taken up only if that is not enough.

112. **The lighting's kernels written once.** Chosen on 2026-11-12, among this, two copies with a
    check of their parity, and one engine's lighting alone. The kernels of the radiance cascades
    stand twice, here and in the sibling, ported by hand, and two faults of one night were found and
    mended in both. They go into the RadianceCascades module, written once in Slang, each engine
    giving its own bindings, so a mend lands in both. Item 265 here and the sibling's item 138.

113. **The order of the three.** Decided on 2026-11-12, they are taken after the dither's grain and
    the blobs in the distance, the two things in view, and the publish, and not beside them nor
    parked. Then 264, the places, then 265, the kernels written once, then 255's trial for 111.

114. **An editor as a module both engines use, later.** The direction of 2026-11-12 is that the
    editor is no focus yet and will be. The aim is a full framework in which ImGui frames for editor
    tools are built easily, with helpers that show data such as the ECS and assets in diagnostics
    windows and a way for a shell to have a surface for an editor layout, a module used by both
    engines, made in ImGui as the sibling's is, giving an engine the functions to build an editor on
    or a way to show its data in one. It is thought through further before it is taken up, so no
    item is made and nothing is built. It refines the split's "no editor", none inside the engine
    and one beside both. Until then the two engines stay on one ImGui binding at one version, and
    the engine's ImGui area and its console stay as they are. Added the same morning, of how it sits
    and of what there is. The editor module provides functions and drawing calls that the engine
    uses in its own ImGui scope, in the same process and as ImGui calls alone. So the engine hosts,
    the module owning no window, no ImGui context and no process. The sibling's editor is not taken
    as the module's design; it is progress to learn from, and the module's own design is set out
    when the module is taken up.

115. **Hardware ray tracing is a backend of the radiance cascades, chosen by what the device can
    do.** Decided on 2026-11-14. The engine stands on SDL3 and Vulkan for modern hardware and
    techniques, so a device that traces rays is used for it. The cascades' rays are traced through
    the meshes' acceleration structures where the device has ray queries and that way is chosen, the
    better picture, and through the scene's distance field elsewhere, on a device that draws on its
    CPU and on the runners among them. The field stays beside the hardware way wherever another part
    of the lighting needs it. Which way a program takes is its choice by a setting, with the
    device's ability as the limit. What each way costs is measured before the default is set. It is
    written once in the shared kernels, after they have moved. Item 271, BevyCSharp Decision 92.

the start (`--parts`), each part a process held to the script's 40 minutes, as the Windows jobs run
theirs. Global illumination's class, the render origin's and the scene field's run in processes of
their own and the rest of the Rendering part in two (`--split
Rendering=2+GlobalIlluminationTests+RenderOriginTests+SceneFieldTests`). The first half takes those
three classes and Graphics (`--only`) and the second every part but those (`--except`), so a part
added later runs in the second, and the first alone plays Slide, publishes it native, follows the
README and builds the first game after its suite, its 75 minutes and the pack run's 120 kept. By the
times the run of `b634f33d` printed on that runner the first half's tests take some 21.5 of the
suite's 37.5 minutes summed, in four processes, and the second some 16 in eighteen. Read here with
`--dotnet` naming a script that lists the tests and runs none, the first half deals the four parts
named and the second the eighteen others, Rendering's two among them. BUILDING.md says how the macOS
jobs run the suite. The scripts', the steps', the validation lines', the package's contents and the
norm tests pass 72 on the workflow as changed.

Item 291, the Bistro as a second scene.

The pack. BevyCSharp's `bistro-exterior.pack` from its scene-packs release, as mended at 08:54, read
310,838,881 bytes with the SHA-256 its manifest names, and `build/make-scene-pack.py` made the
engine's from it with that hash given, its textures' zstd undone and every other file copied,
444,418,983 bytes, SHA-256 68095a0ab80867092404fc5673cd2e4f62605889f131254996a78fb28a42f116, 411
files, the pack on the engine's release since 08:57 in place of the first one of 444,423,270 bytes
made before the mend. `scenes/bistro-exterior.json` carries the bridge's title, source, license and
attribution word for word and names the engine's release. The pack run's scenes job makes both packs
from the bridge's in one loop, each checked against its manifest's size and hash before the upload,
and that loop made the same pack byte for byte here. `./e3d scenes fetch bistro-exterior` fetched it
from the release into an empty folder in 32 s, its hash and every file the same as the pack made
here.

Three faults on the way, one the engine's loader, one the engine's unit, one the pack's.

The loader read no emissive strength. glTF's `KHR_materials_emissive_strength` reaches Assimp as the
material's emissive intensity, which the reader left unread, so the pack's lamps loaded at 1 rather
than 500. The reader multiplies the emissive factor by it, and the test of a lamp at 500 beside a
sign at its factor alone fails without the mend, the lamp reading 1.

A material's emission had no physical unit. `EmissiveIntensity` is a plain strength at the frame's
full scale, 1 the color as the frame's white, which the camera does not change, so a strength of 1
is 1.2 times 2 to the camera's EV100 candelas a square meter, 30,720 under ISO 200, 1/200 s and f/16
and 39,322 under the default EV 15, and the pack's 500 read as some 15 million against the bridge's
500. `ModelMaterial.EmissiveLuminance` gives the color's luminance in candelas a square meter,
multiplied by the camera's pre-exposure as a light given in lux or candelas is, in place of the
plain strength where above 0. Nothing that stands moves, the plain path as it was, the loader
setting no luminance, Sponza keeping its plain 300 and the game setting no camera and giving its
glow blocks plain strengths. The example takes the pack's emission as candelas a square meter, as
the bridge reads it. Its test draws a glass of 500 beside a sign of a plain 2 through a sunny day's
camera and through ISO 800, 1/30 s and f/2, the glass at 500 times each camera's pre-exposure, past
white through the second, and the sign at 2 through both. `docs/materials-light-and-shadows.md` says
what each strength means in one paragraph.

The pack's occlusion was empty. 131 of its 132 materials named their Specular texture as
`occlusionTexture`, the one they named as metallic and rough, and its red, which glTF reads
occlusion from, read under 2 of 255 in all 131 at full size, so every surface's light from all
around was multiplied by 0. At the corner `light.terms` read the probes' indirect light and the
environment at 0.0000 on sunlit and shaded pixels alike, with the field built, and the shade stood
black. The bridge mended it at the source, its pack naming no occlusion texture, and the example's
line leaving the maps out, kept meanwhile, is gone again.

The example. `scenes_bistro` draws the pack alone at the origin, nothing else standing in the 110 by
115 m it takes, its manifest copied beside the program from `scenes/`, and opens without the pack on
the screen Sponza's example opened on, its button fetching it, the screen moved to `ScenePackScreen`
and named by the scene and its manifest. Six views, the bistro's corner as the user's picture frames
it, then the terrace under the string lights, the street to the north-east, the lane behind it, the
round square and the quarter from above, found from a map of the open ground worked out from the
pack's triangles. The field's four cascades of a quarter of a meter reach 16 to 128 m and a far
cascade of 240 holds the quarter from anywhere in it. The camera is metered as Sponza's is, between
EV -1 and 14 and center-weighted, as the user asked, and M holds it at the hour's, ISO 200, 1/50 s
and f/16 while the sun is up, two stops over a sunny day's, the frame the user chose from the
corner's, and ISO 3200, 1/15 s and f/1.4 once it has set. Its help lines say the views, the hour, M
and the flight, as Sponza's do. The examples' table, the gallery and the documents that name
Sponza's example name this one beside it, with a line on the metering and M.

The runs. The strict build is clean, and the focused tests, the model and physical units' tests, the
norm, surface and device surface tests, the scene packs', the cache commands', the documents'
snippets and the emission's render test, pass 95. Both legs of the suite pass 2,512, each in 12
parts of 46 s to 4 m 37 s under the shared lock, every part starting once no exclusive taker had
held the lock, waited for it or kept a file in the waiting folder for 30 s, the first for 180 s, in
64 m 53 s and 71 m 8 s with the waits behind other sessions' timings, the parts themselves 33 m 47 s
and 33 m 30 s, at 2,335 and 2,450 MB at most, the second shuffled by the seed 20261023. The day
camera, the metered start, the occluders and the help and documents' lines went in after the legs,
in the examples and the documents alone, which the legs do not run, and the strict build and the
focused tests pass 95 again after them. The two new tests need no device and no drawn test gives a
luminance, so no leg on three devices was run. They join `E3DModelTests` and `E3DPhysicalUnitsTests`
in their parts on Windows, and no class moves. Every Bistro session held the lock exclusive under
ten minutes and ended its example before letting go, after the two shared ones at 07:52 and 07:58
that filled the card beside the bridge's test.
